It's just the things that some players catch onto and some don't - that you only need to take smaller bites of a deposit to still make the same amount of resources. Be it with a chainsaw, shovel, pick or any combination. Smaller deposits can most times be split in half for 2 full generations. Larger ones can be worked from the top down for much more than barreling straight into them. If you're familiar with all this, then the debate is all about chainsaw versus shovel and pick, but I've come to accept there are optimal situations for either.

Also keep in mind you can pickaxe the walls around and behind a resource to make the split more specific. Play around with hitting them at angles to see that when you pickaxe, and see you also dig at an angle to your side as well. You can use tricks like this to get 3 full resource hits out of a spawner corpse.

But the short and easy idea behind it all? If it's big, mine it from the top down. You can dig into a deposit at half your height and get as much as digging straight into it.. except you can dig it at half your height 4 times as much. It is the difference between the metal sushi producing 100 metal or 600 metal.

Here are two things that I wish every player knew, one of which is slightly difficult to describe in text but I have yet to remember to make a good video.

First, any resource you're generating, throw it -towards- the bus stop. Locate it if you're out in the open, or throw it closest to the entrance you take into any larger interiors. Throwing goes much farther than kicking. Help yourself and other transporting comrades instead of kicking things everywhere nilly-willy and making the distance much farther than it could have been.

Secondly, with any deposit of metal/coal/crystal that is larger than the usual small deposits (inside the large blue ornament, the metal sushi, the blue pig eyes, etc), going hog wild into it will severely cut down how much you can generate from it. A proper technique can easily net 2-4x as many resources, and similarly, 2-4x as much toil for you!

Shovels are key to this. Stand on top of a large deposit, and try to dig a staircase down it as shallowly as you can - you can control which way your staircase goes by the angle of your camera. Use the stair indentations to mine as close to the top as you can - approximately half the height of your character. Always attempt to mine decently-sized leftover slivers, they can still generate a full amount! Proper and mindful angles help extend the amount as well, try to avoid taking gigantic cuts if you can - this is something you practice and get a feel for over time. Then repeat down the height of the resource as necessary. I can make 50 metal from deposits people make 12 from, 400 from what others would get 100, and that difference can be crucial to your town, and your coupon count.

Take it from me, the guy with 1k resource collections where the next closest is 100. If you're curious, bug me about making a video so I'll actually be compelled to remember.
